items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1958-11-14
items.q: I idolized my grandmother. ... I didn't call her grandma, I called her Gagan.

ctx.x: You told me once that she taught you some Senegalese, the African language, a few words.

Because I used to be right by her all the time. I idolized my grandmother. And she spoke her mother's language. But my mother and my aunt and them, they didn't want her yet that. But me, I would be right there by her. And I tell her, Gagan, because I didn't call her grandma, I called her Gagan. I say, Gagan, tell me, tell me. And she would tell me. And sometimes she'd say, Abadra. Abadra, that means good for nothing. That's Senegal.
What was good morning? You told me that, I think, once.
